title: Protocol for evaluating autophagy using LysoTracker staining in the epithelial follicle stem cells of the Drosophila ovary
protocol: Pour 2 mL of Grace’s Insect Medium into the center of a Sylgard-coated petri dish.
Pour a small 1 mL "trash" pool of 1× PBS off-center on the same dish.
Anesthetize female Drosophila melanogaster on the fly pad using CO₂.
Select a female fly with forceps.
Place the selected fly outside the Grace’s medium and gently pin it to the dish.
Quickly detach the head from the thorax to euthanize the fly.
Submerge the fly in the Grace’s medium.
Gently hold the thorax of the submerged fly.
Grasp the posterior abdomen with forceps.
Pull gently until the ovaries slide or pop out, along with intestines.
Remove the sheath (black hair-like fiber bundling the ovary) from the ovaries using forceps.
Gently tease apart the ovaries in a brushing manner with the forceps to release individual ovarioles.
Run the forceps from posterior (egg side) toward the anterior (germarium side) in between adjacent ovarioles to separate the ovarioles and maintain stem cell compartment integrity.
Repeat the dissection process until sufficient ovarioles are collected in Grace's Insect Medium.
Cut off the end of a 200 μL pipette tip for ease of use.
Fill the cut-off tip with approximately 50 μL of Grace’s Insect Medium before collecting the ovarioles.
Pipette small amounts of the medium containing ovarioles to minimize sample loss and sticking to tube walls.
Transfer all collected ovarioles into a labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Tap the tube gently to settle the ovarioles.
Let the tube rest on a rack for 2–3 minutes.
Remove as much liquid as possible once the ovarioles have settled.
Add 200 μL of Lysotracker working stock (1:100) per tube of ovarioles.
Wrap the tube in foil after adding Lysotracker.
Incubate with Lysotracker for 5 minutes.
Wash the ovarioles with 1× PBS once.
Fix the ovarioles by adding 200 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde.
Rock the solution containing ovarioles for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash thrice in 400 μL of PBS + 0.3% Triton (PBST).
Rock for 10 minutes between washes at room temperature.
Let the tissue settle to the bottom of the tube after each wash.
Make a working stock of the primary antibody of interest in PBST + 0.5% BSA.
Add 200–400 μL of primary antibody working stock per tube and rock overnight at 4°C.
Wash thrice with PBST for 10 minutes each.
Remove the PBST, then add working stock of secondary antibody diluted in PBST + 0.5% BSA.
Rock the samples for 2 hours at room temperature.
Incubate for 10 minutes in RNAse A to digest RNA (optional).
Add Draq5 or DAPI (1:1000) in PBST, 100 μL per tube.
Incubate and rock for 10 minutes.
Add 400 μL of PBS and incubate for 5 minutes.
Rock the samples during incubation.
Wash twice with PBS.
Remove as much liquid as possible from the samples.
Add 30 μL of Vectashield per sample and mix thoroughly using a pipette.
Gently transfer the contents to a slide.
Mount with a 22 × 22 #1.5 coverslip.
Place a Kimwipe on top of the cover slip.
Apply gentle pressure to release any bubbles.
Add a weight, such as a half-filled 100 ml glass bottle, on top of the coverslip.
Seal the edges of the cover slip with clear nail polish and dry for at least 5 minutes.
Setup and turn on the lasers for confocal microscopy: use 488 channel (green) for Fas III stained with FITC secondary antibody, and 594 channel (orange) for Lysotracker dye.
Using the 20× objective and the FITC channel, find germaria and focus.
Switch to the 40× oil objective, focus, and move to one end of the slide to start quantifying.
Count the germaria on the slide by going across the slide before slowly moving down and then back across using a sweeping motion.
Switch between the green channel and red channel on the confocal microscope.
Warm up the lasers on the confocal microscope for at least 30 minutes prior to quantification.
Take slides out from short-term or long-term storage before turning on the confocal microscope.
Bring slides to room temperature before starting the experiment.
Quantify Lysotracker within FSCs in region 2A/2B using Fas III staining.
Designate ‘0’ if no FSCs are stained with Lysotracker and ‘1’ if at least one FSC is positively stained with Lysotracker.
Take representative images of germaria that have positively or negatively Lysotracker-stained FSCs.
Harvest ovaries in Grace’s media.
Collect 10 fed female flies or 20 female flies for nutrient restricted conditions and detach as many mature eggs from the ovaries using a 27Gx1/2 needle.
Place detached ovaries in a microcentrifuge tube.
Let ovaries settle to the bottom of the tube for 5 min.
Remove excess liquid from the microcentrifuge tube.
Snap freeze ovaries in liquid nitrogen or using ethanol and dry ice.
Pour ethanol over dry ice in a cryobox to create an ultra-cool liquid pool.
Place tubes containing ovaries into the cold ethanol to ensure uniform freezing.
Add 100 μL of 1× RIPA lysis buffer to each ovary sample in microcentrifuge tubes.
Use a fresh pestle to homogenize ovaries by hand for one minute.
Keep samples on ice during homogenization.
Assemble a 27Gx1/2 needle attached to a 1 mL syringe and suck up lysate.
Shear the sample at least five times with the needle-syringe assembly.
Incubate samples on ice for 15 minutes after shearing.
Spin down the lysate samples at 14,000 RPM (high speed) at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Collect and transfer the supernatant to a labeled microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Determine protein concentration of samples using the Bradford Assay with BSA standard curve.
Based on your protein sample concentration, calculate the volume needed for 10 μg of protein per sample.
Calculate and add the volume of 6× sample buffer required for each sample.
Mix and vortex the samples thoroughly.
Place the samples on a 95°C heat block to denature proteins for 5 minutes.
Setup the vertical gel caster electrophoresis apparatus.
Clamp the glass plates with notched alumina plates and spacer in between on the lower buffer chamber.
Prepare the 10% resolving gel and pour into the stacked plates, filling only three-quarters of each plate.
Allow the resolving gel to polymerize for 45-60 minutes.
Place a comb to prepare the stacking gel once the resolving gel has set.
Pour the stacking gel and allow it to polymerize for 30-45 minutes.
Dilute 10× Running Buffer to 1× concentration.
Fill the cavity between gels with 1× Running Buffer.
Carefully remove the comb using a 27Gx1/2 needle attached to a 1 mL syringe.
Wash each well with the 1× running buffer without applying too much pressure.
Use a p20 pipet to load 5 μL of the protein ladder in the first well.
Place the interlocking safety lid with leads on top of the gel caster chamber, ensuring black is connected to black and red to red.
Hook up electrodes to the electrophoresis power supply unit.
Turn on the power supply and run the gel at 120 Volts for 1.5–2 hours.
Dilute the 10× Transfer Buffer with Methanol to make fresh, 1× Transfer Buffer.
Wear protective PPE when handling Methanol due to its toxicity and flammability.
Dispose of any waste methanol and 1× transfer buffer containing methanol safely according to institutional policies.
Cut 4 pieces of Whatman chromatography paper to the size of the gel.
Cut 1 piece of nitrocellulose membrane to the size of the gel.
Place the nitrocellulose membrane in a plastic dish containing 1× transfer buffer and pre-activate it by soaking in methanol.
Prepare your semi-dry transfer apparatus, forceps, flat spatula, and razor blade.
Pour 1× transfer buffer into plastic dishes for equilibration.
Stop the gel run when the dye front is about 1 mm from the bottom of the gel.
Remove the gel from the caster using a flat spatula to pry open.
Trim the perimeter of the gel with a razor blade.
Place the trimmed gel in a plastic dish containing 1× transfer buffer to equilibrate thoroughly.
Wet two stacked pieces of Whatman paper in transfer buffer and let excess buffer drip out.
Make a transfer sandwich on the base (anode) plate of the semi-dry transfer apparatus.
Sequentially place two wet Whatman Chromatography papers, followed by the pre-activated nitrocellulose membrane, then the gel, and finally two wet Whatman Chromatography papers on top.
Gently squeeze out bubbles using a 15 mL conical tube or wooden pencil between each layer.
Place the cathode plate of the transfer apparatus on top of the anode plate with the sandwich in between.
Perform electro-transfer using 100 mAmps, constant volts for 1.5 hours.
Prepare blocking buffer (5% Milk in TBST) during the transfer process.
Gently open the lid after the transfer is completed.
Cut the membrane into two sections: one between the observed molecular weight of Ref (2)P at 92 kDa and another for ß-actin at 43 kDa.
Make a cut in the upper right corner of each membrane to denote its orientation.
Transfer each membrane from the transfer apparatus to a tray containing 3 mL of blocking buffer using forceps.
Block the membranes for 1 hour at room temperature on a rocker, ensuring they are completely submerged and freely oscillate back and forth.
Dilute Ref (2)P primary antibody in blocking buffer at a concentration of 1:100.
Dilute ß-actin primary antibody in blocking buffer at a concentration of 1:5000.
Incubate membranes with diluted primary antibodies for at least 2 hours or overnight on a rocker at 4°C.
Wash the membranes in 1× TBST thrice for 5 minutes each after incubation with primary antibodies.
Incubate membranes in secondary antibody, anti-Rabbit (1:3000), for Ref (2)P and ß-actin for at least 1 hour.
Wash the membranes in 1× TBST thrice for 5 minutes each after incubation with secondary antibodies.
Prepare chemiluminescence reagents ECL A and B (1:1).
Place a piece of plastic wrap on the bench top and secure it with tape.
Remove excess liquid from membranes by gently dabbing corners on a Kim wipe.
Place the membranes on the saran wrap.
Cover the membranes with ECL and incubate for 1 min at room temperature.
Gently dab excess ECL liquid off membranes on another Kim wipe.
Place the membranes in the X-ray film cassette.
Expose the membrane to X-ray film for an appropriate length of time starting at 30 min.
Gradually decrease exposure time and develop films.
